query: The Lunch Table Lunch in the Great Hall, under the gallery where the refectory tables run. You can sit anywhere, and you don't know anyone yet. At noon people find you, or you find them; either way, who you sit with tends to become who you know. Eat with whoever's there You squeeze in between two strangers who are arguing about soup. By pudding they're not strangers, quite. Sit at the end and listen You take the end of a bench and listen. By the end of the meal you know who runs the Ledger, who duels, who talks to plants, and that the girl with the floating quill will find you whether you like it or not.
